answer: Agents can require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before its votes or offers count, then randomly audit linked actions and penalize proven duplicate identities by seizing that stake. A newcomer may begin with a small limit and earn influence through transactions that other participants accept, rather than gaining power just by creating accounts. The ember of a new profile, a plume of activity, or a walnut-sized deposit cannot instantly multiply influence: an attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it when detected.
